chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Miskān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked him about the minimum amount of tasbīḥ that suffices in rukuʿ and sujud, so he said: three tasbīḥāt.

Thus, the proper way to reconcile these reports is in two ways. One of them is that limiting oneself to a single tasbīḥ is only permissible when it is a specific tasbīḥ, namely saying: “Subḥāna Rabbīya al-ʿAẓīm” in rukuʿ, and “Subḥāna Rabbīya al-Aʿlā” in sujud, according to what is indicated by the narration we transmitted at the beginning of the chapter from Hishām ibn Sālim. But if he says: “Subḥāna Allāh,” then fewer than three repetitions do not suffice for him, as is indicated by that.

key_terms.أَدْنَى: the minimum or least amount that is sufficient
key_terms.التَّسْبِيحِ: the glorification of Allah recited in prayer
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى: the specified glorification recited in sujud
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ: the specified glorification recited in rukuʿ
key_terms.يُجْزِي: is sufficient or valid in fulfilling the requirement

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum tasbīḥ that suffices in rukuʿ and sujud?
ai.summary: This report addresses the minimum tasbīḥ required in rukuʿ and sujud. It explains that one specific formula may suffice once, while the shorter formula “Subḥāna Allāh” must be repeated three times, showing a juristic method of reconciling narrations on salat.
